text.p: Several opposition leaders have been arrested in the West African state of Mali, where the opposition is contesting the reelection of President Alpha Oumar Konare, police sources in the capital said on Monday.

Mountaga Tall of the National Congress for Democratic Initiative (CNID), Almamy Sylla of the Rally for Democracy and Progress (RPD) and Colonel Issouf Traore of the Union of Democratic and Popular Forces (UFDP) had been arrested on suspicion of "inciting violence", the sources added.
They were arrested over the weekend, the sources said.

Mali won widespread praise for its 1992 transition from Moussa Traore's dictatorship to a multi-party system. Military leader Amadou Toumani Toure stepped down after 14 months and now often mediates in regional political crises.
Konare, a historian, won reelection in a May 11 presidential election boycotted by the main opposition. He took the oath of office for a second and final five-year mandate on Sunday.
The opposition boycotted the presidential election demanding the second multi-party elections since the advent of democracy be reorganised after a chaotic April parliamentary election.
The constitutional court annulled the results of that poll but supported Konare's contention that the presidential poll should go ahead before his mandate expired.
About 100 opposition protesters attacked public buildings in the capital on Sunday and destroying equipment at the telecommunications company headquarters.
Konare pledged on Sunday to fight poverty in his arid, landlocked country, and said Mali was on the right track after its first five years of multi-party rule.
